holidays.name: Don't Cry Over Spilled Milk Day
holidays.description: A day for shrugging off life's little messes, from a toppled glass of milk to a spilled latte. It reminds you not to waste tears on small mishaps you can't undo. Grab a paper towel, take a breath and move on. Or pour yourself a fresh glass.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It builds on the old proverb that crying over spilled milk is pointless, and the saying has been around for centuries.
holidays.funFact: The proverb dates back to at least the 1600s. An early version showed up in James Howell's 1659 collection of English proverbs.

holidays.name: Peppermint Patty Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the cool, chocolate-covered, minty-fresh patty. Celebrate by unwrapping one of these round, creamy peppermint candies. It's also a nod to the freckled, sandal-wearing Peanuts character who shares the name.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a candy-lover's holiday that pairs well with the other sweet and quirky days in mid-February.
holidays.funFact: The Peanuts character Peppermint Patty first appeared in the comic strip in 1966. Her real name is Patricia Reichardt.

holidays.name: Satisfied Staying Single Day
holidays.description: A cheerful counterpoint to the Valentine's Day buildup. It celebrates people who are happily flying solo and have no plans to change that. Treat yourself to dinner, a movie or a spontaneous trip, and enjoy your own company.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It appears on the calendar just before Valentine's Day as a day for people who are happy being single.
holidays.funFact: It lands just three days before Valentine's Day, so it works as a small act of rebellion against all the heart-shaped marketing.
